not_covered: NASA ordered Boeing's Starliner to return uncrewed from its first crewed flight because the spacecraft experienced five reaction-control system (RCS) thruster anomalies during the docking approach, and NASA determined that these anomalies could not be guaranteed safe for the deorbit burn since the thrusters could not be ground-tested in their flight condition [Source: ev-1].

This decision meant that astronauts Butch Wilmore and Suni Williams remained on the International Space Station until March 18, 2025, resulting in a stay of roughly 9.5 months compared to the planned ~8 days [Source: ev-1].
